content: 1. Monitor for an increase in adverse effects related to cilostazol when coadministered with cobicistat. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of citalopram by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by interfering with CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response during coadministration with cobicistat. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with anticonvulsants. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clorazepate by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Modify the clorazepate dose if necessary. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of colchicine. Coadministration with colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions. Dosage adjustment of colchicine may be necessary. Refer to colchicine prescribing information for dosing instructions. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 9. Danazol increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dapsone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of darifenacin by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Limit darifenacin to 5 mg orally when coadministered. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of darolutamide. Darolutamide is a substrate of P-gp and CYP3A4. Monitor for increased adverse reactions and adjust the darolutamide dose as needed when coadministered with drugs that are both P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Dosage adjustment of dasatinib may be necessary when coadministered with cobicistat. Refer to dasatinib prescribing information for dosing instructions. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of desipramine by interfering with CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response during coadministration with cobicistat. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diazepam by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. A decreased dose of diazepam may be required. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs. Titrate the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or modify the dosing frequency and continue monitoring. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing docetaxel dosing by 50% if concomitant administration cannot be avoided. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doravirine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of doravirine and CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doxepin by interfering with CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response during coadministration with cobicistat. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elagolix by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for >1 month is not recommended. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of enfortumab vedotin by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Enfortumab vedotin is an antibody-drug conjugate that releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage. MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 in vitro. 29. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the erlotinib dose by 50 mg decrements and monitor for adverse effects. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and toxicities. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ethosuximide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of felodipine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flecainide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response during coadministration with SSRIs and cobicistat. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels of fluticasone furoate by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels of fluticasone inhaled by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors that are not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 44. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of cobicistat. Carefully titrate the dose of antidepressants to the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response during coadministration with SSRIs and cobicistat. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib’s major active metabolite). Monitor for toxicities that may require fostamatinib dose reduction. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels of gefitinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations and result in potentially fatal respiratory depression. 50. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites and reduce its efficacy. 51. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imipramine. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response during coadministration.
